supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41 UTC, ian.doyle logged on to WS-ZADAMS-01 over the network from 10.55.10.23, and the session received special privileges. This is consistent with the organization’s stated remote workstation-patching practice.
At 13:42 UTC, PowerShell ran as ian.doyle with the command line pointing to the documented patch script, \\FILE-SUN-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1.

The PowerShell process was followed by Windows Update traffic and a wusa process installing a Windows update package, corroborating a patching task rather than establishing suspicious PowerShell activity.

The recorded PowerShell process ended about seven seconds after it started, consistent with the report that a PowerShell window appeared briefly; the logs do not establish whether a window was visibly displayed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process records show the patch-script path but not the script contents or whether that file was unchanged and approved at execution time (T244-00119, T244-00120).
The available process records establish PowerShell execution and its duration, but do not establish whether the user saw a window (T244-00119, T244-00128, T244-00129).
The source address for ian.doyle's network logon is recorded, but these records do not identify its hostname (T244-00110, T244-00111).
claims_not_established: Whether the contents of the patch script matched the approved script at the time it ran (T244-00119, T244-00120).
Whether the PowerShell process created a visible window for zoe.adams (T244-00119, T244-00128, T244-00129).
unrelated_findings: Separately investigate Meridian OpsAgent: an unapproved agent ran on WS-ZADAMS-01 and made an explicit-credential logon attempt using svc-ledger. This is outside the alerted PowerShell activity (T244-00227, T244-00228, T244-00235, T244-00236, T244-00237).

Separately review the connection to updates.paloaltonetworks.com with a GlobalProtect user agent. The record shows a connection, not that a VPN or remote-access session was established; this is outside the alerted PowerShell activity (T244-00006).
